parts.text: What is the company's bereavement leave policy?

Under the company's Bereavement Leave Policy, eligible employees may take up to 5 consecutive paid working days off for the loss of an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent, sibling) and up to 3 paid working days for extended family members. Additional unpaid time may be requested through your manager. For full details and formal submission guidelines, please refer to the [Bereavement Leave Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/bereavement-leave).

Employees are eligible for up to 5 paid days for immediate family members and 3 paid days for extended family members under the Bereavement Leave Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/bereavement-leave).

property.description: The model response must explicitly mention 5 paid days for immediate family and 3 paid days for extended family.
The response must include a grounded citation link to the Bereavement Leave Policy document.

parts.text: Are employees allowed to expense noise-canceling headphones?

Yes. Under the [Remote Work & Expense Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/expense-guidelines#peripherals), full-time remote and hybrid employees are eligible for a one-time reimbursement of up to $150 for noise-canceling headphones or equivalent audio equipment used for work calls. Claims must be submitted via Concur with itemized receipts within 60 days of purchase.

Full-time remote and hybrid employees can expense up to $150 for noise-canceling headphones under the Remote Work & Expense Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/expense-guidelines#peripherals).

property.description: The response must state the $150 reimbursement limit for remote/hybrid employees with a valid policy citation.

parts.text: What equipment is provided under the remote work policy for home office setup?

According to the [Remote Work Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/remote-work-policy#equipment), designated remote employees are eligible for standard enterprise IT equipment: one laptop, up to two external 27-inch monitors, a docking station, and a one-time $250 ergonomic accessory stipend. Requests must be placed via ServiceImmediately IT hardware catalog.

Remote employees receive a company laptop, up to two 27-inch external monitors, a docking station, and a $250 accessory stipend per the Remote Work Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/remote-work-policy#equipment).
Can I accept a gift basket from a vendor partner?

Per the [Code of Conduct & Ethics Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/code-of-conduct#gifts), employees may only accept perishable or promotional gifts valued at under $50 USD. Any gift exceeding $50, or any cash or cash equivalents (gift cards), must be politely declined or reported to the Ethics & Compliance Office.

Employees may accept gifts under $50 USD. Gifts over $50 or cash equivalents are prohibited and must be declared to Ethics & Compliance per Code of Conduct (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/code-of-conduct#gifts).

I need to take 3 weeks off for medical treatment. What leave should I use?

For medical leave lasting 3 consecutive weeks, several options apply depending on your medical certification:
1. **Short-Term Disability (STD)**: Covers continuous medical leave beyond 5 consecutive working days at 70-100% salary ([Short-Term Disability Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/disability-benefits)).
2. **Family & Medical Leave Act (FMLA)**: Provides job-protected leave for qualifying serious health conditions ([FMLA Guidelines](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/fmla-leave)).
3. **Accrued Sick Leave**: Can be utilized for the initial 5-day waiting period prior to STD activation ([Sick Leave Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/leave-policy#sick)).

What is my annual limit for outpatient sick leave, and how quickly must I submit an MC if I am out sick for 3 days?

Under the [Outpatient Sick Time & Hospitalization Leave Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/sick-leave):
- **Outpatient Sick Leave Limit**: Eligible employees receive up to **14 days** of paid outpatient sick leave per calendar year.
- **Medical Certificate (MC) Submission**: Because you are out sick for more than two work days (3 days), you must submit a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner via WorkWeek within **48 hours** of taking the leave.

Eligible employees receive up to 14 days of paid outpatient sick leave per year. An MC is required within 48 hours for absences exceeding two work days under the Outpatient Sick Time & Hospitalization Leave Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/sick-leave).

property.description: The response must state that the outpatient sick leave limit is 14 days per calendar year.
The response must specify the 48-hour submission deadline for medical certificates when out sick for more than 2 days.

parts.text: I work 12-hour shifts and have been at Altostrat for 8 years. How many vacation days do I earn per year, and how many days of leave do I log for taking one shift off?

Under the [Paid Vacation Leave Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/vacation-leave):
- **Annual Vacation Accrual**: With 8 years of continuous service (falling in the 7 to 10 years tier), you accrue **21 days** of paid vacation per year.
- **Shift Conversion**: Shift workers log leave based on standard 8-hour blocks. Taking a single **12-hour shift** off requires recording **1.5 vacation days** in WorkWeek.

Employees with 8 years of tenure earn 21 days of vacation per year, and taking one 12-hour shift off requires logging 1.5 vacation days under the Paid Vacation Leave Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/vacation-leave).

property.description: The response must state the correct vacation accrual for 8 years of service.
The response must specify that a single 12-hour shift corresponds to 1.5 vacation days.

parts.text: Can you explain the rules regarding pay and working hours during the 2-week Ramp-Back period when returning from family leave?

Under the [Ramp-Back Time Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/ramp-back):
- **Duration**: Up to 2 weeks immediately following return from at least 10 weeks of family/bonding leave.
- **Working Hours**: You must work a minimum of **50% hours in week 1** and **75% hours in week 2**.
- **Compensation**: You receive **100% of your normal salary** throughout the entire 2-week ramp-back transition.
During the 2-week Ramp-Back period, employees work 50% hours in week 1, 75% hours in week 2, and receive 100% pay under the Ramp-Back Time Policy (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/ramp-back).

property.description: The response must explain working 50% hours in week 1, 75% in week 2, and receiving 100% pay.

parts.text: I stayed at my cousin's house in Sydney during a business trip. Can I expense a $45 gift card as a thank-you present?

No, you cannot expense the gift card. Under the [Travel & Expense Guidelines](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/travel-expenses) and Code of Conduct, gift cards, cash equivalents, and personal thank-you gifts are strictly non-reimbursable expenditures, even when staying with family or friends during business travel.
Clean refusal explaining that gift cards and personal thank-you gifts are non-reimbursable under Travel & Expense Guidelines (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/travel-expenses).
I want to take a potential client to a room salon for $80 per person. Since this is under the $100 entertainment limit, am I allowed to do this?

No, this is strictly prohibited. Under Section 5.2 of the [Code of Conduct & Ethics Policy](https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/code-of-conduct), business entertainment must never involve adult entertainment venues (including room salons, hostess bars, and strip clubs) or gambling. There is a zero-tolerance prohibition on these venues regardless of the cost per person or the standard $100 pre-approval threshold.

Strict ethical refusal: Room salons and adult entertainment venues are completely banned for client entertainment regardless of the amount under the Code of Conduct (https://hr.enterprise.internal/policies/code-of-conduct).
